summary_html: Youth remains in **extended foster care** or receives **transitional services** after age 18 under federal programs promoting independence.
authority_html:
- **Chafee Foster Care Independence Act (CFCIA)** — independent-living and transition funding  
- **FCSIAA** — extends care to age 21 with education and housing supports

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed a disposition order requiring a father to complete a domestic violence assessment, holding that once a child is adjudicated dependent the juvenile court has continuing jurisdiction and may impose any condition on a parent that is reasonable, proportionate, and calculated to serve the child's best interest.
key_cases.relevance: Its holding on the juvenile court's continuing jurisdiction over an adjudicated child is the nearest Utah authority to extended-jurisdiction questions for older youth.
key_cases.quote: Under section 78A-6-117(2), the juvenile court may impose conditions on a parent so long as the conditions are "reasonable."

key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed, holding that the juvenile court had subject matter jurisdiction because the mother voluntarily placed K.F. in state custody, that the order ending reunification and setting a goal of individualized permanency was final and appealable and appropriate where compelling reasons ruled out reunification, adoption, guardianship and kinship placement, and that the juvenile court's findings on service-plan compliance and on DCFS's reasonable efforts were owed broad discretion and were not clearly in error.
key_cases.relevance: Its approval of long-term, potentially permanent foster care as a permanency goal is the closest Utah Supreme Court authority to the position of a youth who will remain in care rather than exit to a family.
key_cases.quote: appellate courts defer to juvenile courts on matters of credibility, and juvenile courts have broad discretion in determining whether reasonable reunification efforts were made

search_keywords: Utah Division of Child and Family Services

state_agency.name: Utah Division of Child and Family Services

extended_foster_care_age: To age 21, only while the juvenile court orders DCFS to keep serving the young adult (Utah Code 80-1-102(56)(b)(i); 78A-6-120(1)(a)). A young adult who is 18 or older but younger than 21 and in DCFS custody on abuse, neglect, or dependency grounds may petition the juvenile court to be removed from division custody, and the court reviews that petition within 14 days; if removed, the young adult may petition within 90 days to re-enter division custody, and the juvenile court shall order the division to take custody (Utah Code 80-3-503)

common_failures: Failure to prove unfitness by clear and convincing evidence
Santosky v. Kramer standard not met

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Must file TPR or document compelling reason
